title: Salary negotiation basics
examples: What is the best way to find out what someone else in this job makes?
Should I mention my current salary when I negotiate a new job?
What should I focus on when they talk about my total package?

explain.say: First you must do thorough research on the role.

items: Look at job boards for salary data.
Talk to people already in that role.

explain.say: Next you need to understand the typical salary ranges.
Always consider the total compensation package details.
For example if the job offers a base salary and a bonus structure you must calculate the total.
In a real job interview you must combine your research with the total package view.
A common mistake is only focusing on the base salary amount.

faq.q: Should I name a specific number when I am asked for my desired salary?
faq.a: It is often better to provide a researched range rather than one single number. You can also try to get the employer to state the range first. You might ask, "What is the established salary band for this role?" or "Can you share the compensation range for this position?"
asks: What number should I give them?
Is a range better than one number?

faq.q: How do I research salary information accurately for a new industry?
faq.a: Use multiple reliable sources like industry reports or professional networking sites. Cross-referencing data helps you build a strong, defensible range. You could also ask, "What benchmarks do you use for salary setting?" or "Are there industry standards I should be aware of?"
asks: Where do I find salary data?
Are job boards reliable for salary info?

faq.q: What is the difference between base salary and total compensation?
faq.a: Base salary is just the fixed money you earn before extras. Total compensation includes that base plus bonuses, stock, and benefits. You should always calculate the total value to compare offers fairly. You could ask, "How is the total compensation structured?" or "What does the full benefits package include?"

faq.q: If I am currently underpaid, how should I bring that up?
faq.a: Frame it around market value for the role, not just your past pay. You can state that your research suggests the market rate is higher. Try saying, "Based on my experience and market research, I was expecting a figure closer to X." or "I am looking for compensation aligned with senior roles in this field."
asks: Should I mention my old salary?
How do I address a pay gap?

faq.q: Should I negotiate everything at once or in stages?
faq.a: It is usually best to address compensation after you have secured mutual interest in the role. Focus first on understanding the full scope of the job. You might wait until the final interview stage to discuss salary, or ask, "What is the timeline for discussing compensation?"
asks: When should I talk about money?
Should I wait until the last meeting?

facts: Salary negotiation is a professional skill that requires preparation.
Total compensation includes base salary, bonuses, and benefits.
Researching market rates provides objective data for your negotiation.
A salary range is often more effective than a single desired number.

quiz.say: A candidate researches that the market rate for a role is between seventy thousand and ninety thousand dollars. Which action best demonstrates using this research?

options.show: Saying you want the highest number possible.
options.say: Saying you want the highest number possible.

options.show: Saying you want the lowest number in the range.
options.say: Saying you want the lowest number in the range.

options.show: Stating a target range within the researched band.
options.say: Stating a target range within the researched band.

options.show: Asking for exactly ninety thousand dollars.
options.say: Asking for exactly ninety thousand dollars.

quiz.why: Providing a range shows flexibility while anchoring your value to market data.

wrong.0: This can appear greedy and disregards the established market norms.
wrong.1: This undervalues your skills and the role you are applying for.
wrong.3: This is too high and might seem unrealistic without justification.

quiz.say: When evaluating an offer, why is considering paid time off (PTO) important?

options.show: You should only focus on the salary number.
options.say: You should only focus on the salary number.

options.show: PTO is a tangible benefit that adds value beyond the base salary.
options.say: PTO is a tangible benefit that adds value beyond the base salary.

options.show: It is not money, so it does not count.
options.say: It is not money, so it does not count.

options.show: It is only relevant for full-time jobs.
options.say: It is only relevant for full-time jobs.

quiz.why: Benefits like PTO represent paid time that has monetary value to your overall package.

wrong.0: Ignoring benefits means you are only seeing part of the employer's full offer.
wrong.2: PTO is compensated time, which is a measurable part of your total value.
wrong.3: Many benefits are structured to be valuable regardless of employment status.
